Subject: Performance SLO qualification  post-call recap & next steps

Hi Alex / Priya 

Thanks again for joining the call today  good sync. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of your goals:
- Primary SLO: p95 latency <= 300ms for single-shot summary requests (avg response length ~64 tokens)
- Peak throughput target: 250 QPS for inference-only endpoints (daytime peak); baseline sustained traffic ~80 QPS
- Target concurrency (simultaneous requests): ~40 active connections
- Streaming: need first-token streaming within 50ms for UX (progressive summary display)
- SLA needs: 99.9% availability for the inference API in us-east region

What we propose as next steps:
1) Technical follow-up with Rishi to map to configuration options (batching, caching, model variant, quantization)  propose Tue 2026-12-08 16:00 ET.
2) You to share a small traffic sample (CSV) + typical payload sizes so we can model token costs  received (thanks) as attachment 'novaretail-traffic-sample.csv'.
3) Redwood to deliver a short SLO proposal with cost/perf levers and a recommended runbook for a 2-hour load test. Draft attached: 'redwood-slo-proposal-v1.pdf'.

Initial recommendations (high level):
- Continuous batching with 15-30ms batching window tuned to reduce per-token cost without violating the 50ms first-token streaming target.
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated contextual prefixes (store warm KV across requests where applicable).
- Quantization: recommend int8/LLM.int8 for primary model to reduce GPU memory and increase throughput; keep a float16 variant for quality-sensitive edge cases.
- Model variants: start with a mid-sized Llama-3-compatible variant for cost/latency balance; have a smaller low-cost variant as fallback during spikes.

Please confirm Tue 12/8 for the tech call or suggest an alternate time. If you want, we can run a quick synthetic load test next week to validate the streaming-first-token behavior.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole

(415) 555-0147

Perfect  thanks for the percentile data, Alex. Meeting is on the calendar for Tue 2026-12-08 16:00 ET (invite sent).

A few pre-work asks so Rishi can size the config before the call: 
1) Can you share approximate tokens per request distribution (we have percentiles but need tokens per request mapping)  if the percentile doc maps to bytes we can convert, otherwise a simple column in the CSV with token_estimate is fine.
2) Do you expect burst patterns longer than 30 minutes (brand campaigns often produce multi-hour elevated traffic)? If yes, what's the worst-case sustained QPS for an hour?
3) Are you routing through any CDN or edge proxy that terminates streaming connections? We need to know if we can rely on persistent TCP connections for streaming.

Preliminary operational plan we'll discuss:
- Baseline model variant: L3-mid (FP16) with int8 quantized candidate for production once validated; fallback to L3-small for extreme peak mitigation.
- Batching window: adaptive continuous batching tuned to keep mean latency under 220ms while meeting first-token <50ms for streaming.
- Cache policy: KV cache for user profile prefixes + short-term prefix cache (TTL ~5 mins) for repeat requests.
- Load test: 2-hour soak at 1.2x expected peak (300 QPS) with synthetic token distribution including long-tail 256-token requests.

Rishi  can you sketch the config items you'll bring to the call (GPU type, batch window ranges, cache sizing assumptions, quantization risks)?

Thanks  look forward to the call.

Marissa

Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification  pre-call notes and config sketch

Hi all 

I took a pass at a concise config sketch based on Marissa/Alex notes and the traffic sample. High-level notes for the call: 

1) Hardware baseline: A100S or equivalent per-serving cluster for predictable FP16 throughput. We can also run int8 builds on Ampere or Hopper-class hardware with better memory footprint for higher concurrency.

2) Batching strategy: Continuous batching with adaptive windowing  start with a 15ms micro-batch window and allow expansion up to 40ms during low-latency slack to improve amortized throughput. For streaming we ensure the first-token path bypasses long waits (first-token fence at 20-50ms).

3) Caching: KV cache for session-context and prefix cache for repeated product/user combos. Cache sizing: estimate 15-20GB of KV cache for 200k active users; TTL tuning will be critical (5-15 minutes typically).

4) Quantization & model variants: Recommend int8-lora-quantized primary for production after validation; keep fp16 variant live for A/B quality checks and fallbacks. For spikes, auto-fallback to L3-small (quantized) to preserve latency with higher throughput headroom.

5) Streaming considerations: If a proxy interrupts chunked transfer encoding we may need to route streaming through a passthrough gateway. Confirm Alex whether your CDN/proxy preserves chunked streaming. If not, we can front with a lightweight edge that keeps the connection open to Redwood runtime.

6) Cost levers: primary levers are batch window sizing, switching model variants (L3-mid -> L3-small during spikes), and enabling int8 quantization. Caching cuts token compute for repeated prefixes significantly. We'll quantify cost delta in the proposal doc before the load test.

7) Load test plan: 2-hour soak at 300 QPS with token distribution that includes 5% 256-token requests. Also include a spike test: 5-minute 1,000 QPS burst to validate graceful degradation and fallback behavior.

I'll bring a short dashboard template for expected metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, first-token latency, CPU/GPU utilization, batch sizes, cache hit rate).

See you Tue.

Rishi
